expected_evidence: Geological: ocean/lake sediment core proxies (δ18O foraminifera, IRD, grain-size) showing reduced North Atlantic Deep Water formation coincident with a glacial meltwater discharge event (e.g., Lake Agassiz drainage routed via St. Lawrence or Mackenzie corridors) at the Younger Dryas onset (~12.9 ka)
Geological: Greenland/Antarctic ice-core records (δ18O, dust, methane) documenting the abrupt Younger Dryas cooling consistent with AMOC slowdown
Geological: varved lake sediment chronologies and 'black mat' stratigraphic horizons in North America marking the extinction/climate transition

Genetic: ancient DNA and phylogenetic bottleneck/coalescent analyses of North American megafauna (mammoth, horse, camel, short-faced bear) showing population decline or collapse timing clustering near the YD boundary
Material/archaeological: radiocarbon-dated megafaunal last-appearance datasets and faunal assemblage turnover in North American sites bracketing the interval

Model-prior (low-tier, from training): general familiarity with the 'meltwater pulse/Broecker hypothesis' linking glacial lake outburst floods to AMOC weakening and Younger Dryas cooling, and its contested overlap with megafaunal extinction and human-overkill debates
response.rationale: The hypothesis ties a specific mechanism (AMOC shutdown from a meltwater pulse) to megafaunal extinction in North America across an interval that straddles the Upper Paleolithic and Younger Dryas periods (roughly 21,000-11,000 years ago). The relevant evidentiary channels are overwhelmingly geological (ice cores, marine/lake sediment isotopic and grain-size proxies) and genetic (ancient DNA bottleneck signatures), with material/archaeological (radiocarbon-dated faunal turnover) as secondary support. Per the detectability table, geological (0.6-0.65) and to a lesser extent material (0.35) and genetic (0.25-0.3) evidence for this era have non-trivial but modest survival/discoverability, while textual, linguistic, oral_tradition, and iconographic channels are essentially inapplicable (values 0.0-0.1) for a pre-literate, pre-iconographic causal-climate claim. Astronomical detectability is listed high (0.7) but this largely reflects dating-calibration utility (varve/radiocarbon chronometry) rather than direct evidence of the causal claim itself, so I weight it lightly. Because ice-core and marine-sediment records of the Younger Dryas cooling and meltwater discharge are well-documented in the paleoclimate literature (model-prior, unverified against the actual evidence corpus here), and megafaunal extinction chronologies have been extensively radiocarbon-dated, this kind of correlational/mechanistic evidence plausibly has survived and been found. However, 'corroborated' implies a settled causal link, whereas the actual scientific literature treats AMOC-shutdown-as-driver-of-extinction as one contested hypothesis among competing explanations (human overkill, direct climate stress, impact hypothesis), so absence of a definitive causal smoking gun should not be read as falsity — it reflects the genuine difficulty of establishing causation (vs. correlation) from proxy records this old, compounded by only moderate detectability scores across the dominant evidence types (geological ~0.6-0.65, genetic ~0.25-0.3, material ~0.35). I suggest a blended detectability adjustment of ~0.45, weighted toward geological evidence as the primary plausible channel, with genetic and material as supporting but weaker channels, and near-zero contribution from textual/linguistic/oral/iconographic channels for this period.
